tweets.title: ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation (@GoogleDeepMind)
tweets.text:
🧵[1/7] Excited to share our new research from @GoogleDeepMind 

ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation

Introducing a highly parameter-efficient class of visual generative models
1. High Throughput
2. Elastic/Any-Time Inference

🧵[2/7] Deep generative models usually stack unique layers = massive parameter bloat.

Instead, what if we reuse layers?

By looping them, ELT slashes parameters but maintain high generation quality!

🧵[3/7] Training loops can be unstable. Our fix? Intra-Loop Self Distillation (ILSD).

We jointly optimize the max-loop output (teacher) and intermediate loops (student) in one step.

This forces consistency and stabilizes the entire deep recurrent structure.

🧵[4/7] The best part? "Any-Time" Inference. ⚡

ILSD gives us a family of elastic models from a single training run.

You can dynamically dial your compute/loops up or down at inference time to balance speed vs. quality.

🧵[5/7] ELT delivers faster training convergence (up to 2.0x speedup)

🧵[6/7] Results: Under iso-inference-compute, ELT gets a 4x param reduction while hitting:

FID of 2.0 (ImageNet 256)
FVD of 72.8 (UCF-101)

Check out the full paper for all the details! 👇
🔗

🧵[7/7] Huge thanks to my amazing co-authors and collaborators for their insights and contributions! 👏
@Swayam_421 @adityakusupati @paul_sujoy_ @gautham_ga_ @jainprateek_

tweets.text:
Wanted to share my interview experience with Proximal (recently in June-July)

Round 1:  RL coding round (LLMs not allowed): My background is mostly in pretraining, vision and efficiency. This round slightly caught me off guard. Relied on core logic and whatever RL basics I knew. Thought I performed average and failed, but moved forward, likely thanks to my prev experience and background.

Round 2: Take Home Assignment (Paid) - Building a benchmark for web design replication. Needed to complete it in 2-3 days. 

Now a bit annoying part comes...
So now had to present the assignment to an interviewer. It felt very disengaged. I think interviewer was just busy doing his own work during the call. After that call, I followed up several times, but there was hardly any response from their side. Yeah after several weeks, got the "not proceeding" message. Communication could definitely improve here.

Now, need to give credit, where its due. They had a good set of interviews, instead of generic LeetCode/DSA etc.
I learnt something while preparing or doing assignment.

tweets.title: MaGNeTS: Generating High-Quality Images/Videos 3× Faster Without Extra Parameters via Decode-Time Scaling & KV Caching
tweets.text:
Can we generate high-quality images/videos 3× faster without extra parameters? 🤯

Our latest work “MaGNeTS” rethinks compute efficiency in generative models using decode time model scaling & KV caching!

Parallel Decoding of discrete tokens (MaskGIT) reduces compute of autoregressive methods significantly, but it still includes several redundant computations.

Not all sampling steps need the same model capacity.
KV-caching can boost parallel decoding too, when refreshed smartly!

Unmaksed token density visualization across sampling steps reveals structured unmasking.
💡 Smarter decoding = Faster generation!

🔍 How tokens evolve during generation!

Early steps: Background region of ImageNet
Later steps: Middle of the image

Less compute, same quality!

Applying guidance only in the final few sampling steps is sufficient⚡
Fewer guided steps → Efficient inference ✅

More insights? Dive deep into the paper

Huge thanks to my amazing co-authors and collaborators for their insights and contributions! 👏
@paul_sujoy_ @DebapriyaTula @gaganjain1582 @jainprateek_ @doktorshenoy
and thanks for the support @ManishGuptaMG1

tweets.title: Can we use different-sized models in different stages of diffusion inference for efficient generation?
tweets.text:
Can we use different-sized models in different stages of diffusion inference for efficient generation?
Some initial inference-time experiments on UVIT () in the thread👀

Models used:   pre-trained checkpoints of UViT on ImageNet64×64, U-ViT-L/4  and U-ViT-M/4
Sampling steps: 50
(All exp on single A100 GPU)

Now what is the optimal model schedule?
Initial  denoising steps play a crucial role in shaping the final output of the reverse diffusion process, so utilizing the L model for the early stages and transition to the M model for the later denoising steps.

For similar experiments, checkout our recent ICML paper, MaGNeTS: Masked Generative Nested Transformers with Decode Time Scaling ()

tweets.title: Nice work! few ques — 1. would comparing at matched latency be fairer than NFE alone? cfg's two branches…
tweets.text:
Nice work! few ques

1. would comparing at matched latency be fairer than NFE alone? cfg's two branches can be batched/stacked together to reduce latency, but correction passes are sequential.

2. Also, this work gives me a feel of early-exit training i.e. supervising intermediate representations too with the ground truth and maybe with distillation too? So won't the deeper denoiser (D28) ablation done in Table 7 would be better, if we also apply intermediate supervision at say D14? 

3. Then, to isolate the contribution further, you'd want to compare hidden state continuation against decoding and reembedding that intermediate image, and ablate stop grad?

tweets.text: "Compared to Looped-DiT which needs deep supervision on every loop iteration during training" - I am not sure if they need deep supervision at every loop iteration in every training iteration. Thats what they have used in the paper, but I dont think they have ablated this. Randomly sampling a loop depth and just supervising that might also work as well. which we do in our Elastic Looped transformers () work
